designSummary: Multiple-baseline interrupted time series with staggered starts: Hospital A in January, B in April, C in July and D in October 2027; monthly catheter days per ward from each hospital's baseline to March 2028.
sampleSize: Twelve wards contribute about 300 ward-months. With four hospitals starting at three-month intervals and at least 11 baseline months each, the retrieved simulation shows about 80 percent power to detect a 25 percent level change, against about 55 percent for a simultaneous start (c4). With a baseline near 19 catheter days per 100 patient days, a 25 percent change is a fall to about 14, similar to the published multi-hospital result (c1). Infections, at about 2 per 1,000 catheter days, give too few events for any test and are described only.
primaryAnalysis: Segmented Poisson regression of monthly catheter days with patient days as the offset, hospital-specific change points at each start, hospital-specific levels (so Hospital D's point-count series has its own level), ward random effects, calendar month terms for seasonality and a first-order autoregressive error. The main estimate is the average level change across hospitals; the concurrent comparison with hospitals not yet started is shown alongside.
secondaryAnalysis: Sensitivity analysis excluding Hospital D; descriptive infection rates per 1,000 catheter days; run charts of indication documentation and reinsertion by age group.
missingData: Months with incomplete flowsheet extracts or missed point counts are flagged and excluded, never imputed; Hospital D's data enter the pooled model only after its information governance agreement.
multiplicity: One primary estimate; secondary and balancing measures are descriptive.
software: R; model code and change points archived before Hospital A starts.
overfittingGuards: Change points fixed by the coach schedule before any data are seen
Hospital D's series never switches measurement source
summary: Staggered multiple-baseline analysis with hospital-specific change points; about 80 percent power for a 25 percent level change.
